items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: And I loved Stevie Wonder of course, Aretha, the Temptations, the Four Tops, and I got a chance then to play with all these people when I was older.

ctx.x: I was. I grew up in Michigan and my father played the trumpet and my mother played piano. I had three sisters, they all took piano lessons. And it’s funny because my father also worked at a factory, as many people in Michigan did, but on the weekends played gigs. So when I was a little kid he would take me to his gigs, so I was like really small. And I would go and he usually had a band of one or two saxophones in the band, piano and/or accordion, bass, drums, guitar, you know, and so he would sing and play the…

one of his saxophone players so he was pushing me more towards hey, maybe — would you like to play the saxophone. So one day he brought a saxophone home like you know for a birthday or something like that. And I was quite young so I was starting to sit in with him when I was ten years old. So I was already curious about the music that he played, which was mostly older music like the swing era, like old jazz standards. But then he would also incorporate a couple of rock tunes, because younger people would want to…

just trying to get that vibe. She came in, “What are you playing? That’s just nonsense” you know because I was just improvising. And because she said that it was like oh yeah well then I would do more.
